chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Khayran al-Khadim who said:

I wrote to the Man (peace be upon him) asking him about the garment that is hit by wine and the flesh of the pig, 'Can one pray in it or not?' For our companions have differed regarding it, so some of them said, 'Pray in it, for Allah has only prohibited its drinking,' and some of them said, 'Do not pray in it.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Do not pray in it, for it is filth.'

He said, 'And I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who lends his garment to the one whom he knows eats the catfish or drinks wine, and he returns it. Can he pray in it before washing it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot pray in it until he washes it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in clothes soiled by wine or pork?
ai.summary: This hadith resolves the juristic dispute regarding garments soiled by wine or pork by establishing their status as *rijs* (impurity), thereby requiring washing before prayer. It distinguishes between the prohibition of consumption and the physical impurity of the substance, while also addressing the specific case of lending garments to known sinners, emphasizing that mere exposure to the impurity necessitates purification before valid worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Khayran Al Khadim who said,

‘I wrote to the Imamasws asking himasws about the clothes hit by the wine and the flesh of swine, ‘Can Salāt be prayed in these, for our companions have differed with regards to it. So some of them are saying, ‘You can pray Salāt in these for Allahazwj, rather, has Prohibited its drinking’, and some of them are saying, ‘You cannot pray Salāt in it’. So heasws wrote: ‘You cannot pray Salāt in it, for it is filth’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the one who lends his cloth to the one whom he knows that he eats the catfish, or drinks the wine. So he returns it. Can he pray Salāt in it before he washes it?’ Heasws said: ‘He cannot pray Salāt in it until he washes it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Khayran al-Khadim who has said the following: “I once wrote to the man, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asking him about clothes which come in contact with wine and flesh of pig, if I can perform Salah (prayer) wearing such cloth or not. Our people have differences on the issue. Certain ones say, ‘You can perform Salah (prayer) with it because only drinking is unlawful.’ Certain others say, ‘You must not perform Salah (prayer) wearing them.’ He (the Imam) wrote, ‘You must not perform Salah (prayer) wearing them: it is rijs (filthy).’

I then asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about someone who borrows clothes from one whom he knows consumes al- Jirry (scale-less fish) or drinks wine. He then returns what he has borrowed. Can he perform Salah (prayer) wearing them before washing? He (the Imam) said, ‘He does not perform Salah (prayer) wearing them before washing.’”
